title: BalLOT: Balanced k-means clustering with optimal transport
summary: The paper formulates balanced k-means as alternating minimization over an optimal-transport coupling, yielding BalLOT, which replaces Lloyd assignment with a rectangular transportation problem. It proves integrality, average-landscape optimality, and one-step planted-cluster recovery guarantees under balanced mixture/stochastic ball models, including a k=2 diameter-initialization threshold Δ>2√2. Numerical experiments compare exact BalLOT, entropic BalLOT, Lloyd, replicated-centroid matching, and an SDP on synthetic data.

match_target.why: This is the user's hinted central result and is cheaper than SDP/full convergence experiments: it needs only synthetic k=2 data, a diameter-initialized exact transportation assignment, and a one-step partition check.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the paper reports no repeated-run std for the Δ threshold and separation is an unbounded value, so use 10% relative tolerance around 2√2.

requirements.stmt: Represent the assignment by a coupling F on the transportation polytope U_{n,k}, with nonnegative entries, row sums 1/n, and column sums 1/k.
requirements.quote: The row constraints distribute the mass 1/n of each data point among the cluster labels

requirements.stmt: Use squared Euclidean distances C_ij=||x_i−μ_j||^2 as the assignment cost; do not use unsquared distances.
requirements.cite: Section 1.2, equation (4) and Kantorovich cost discussion
requirements.quote: In our setting, a = 1 n1n, b = 1 k1k, and Cij = ∥xi −μj∥2.

requirements.stmt: After each assignment, update centroids by μ^{t+1}=k X F^{t+1}.
requirements.quote: Differentiating with respect to the centroids gives that the unique minimizer is μ = kXF

requirements.stmt: For full BalLOT runs, stop when the Frobenius norm ||μ^{t+1}−μ^t||_F is below the chosen tolerance.
requirements.quote: We terminate once ∥μt+1−μt∥F is below a prescribed tolerance.
